plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on the researcher Eric Weinstein, tells of a 1957 physics conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, where the study of quantum gravity, the attempt to join gravity with the physics of tiny particles, got its start. He says an Austrian mathematician there named Hermann Bondi talked about negative mass, a strange kind of matter that would behave the opposite way to normal matter under gravity. Michels raises it because, if the idea held, it could point toward new ways of moving craft.
